X018.title: Click granularity guard, onCellClick, and stale mouse-target revalidation
X018.why: The host needs single-cell fullscreen clicks for click-to-expand. Double-click selection must remain native word selection, and single-click handling must not duplicate clipboard feedback. Pointer events must also never reach a stale target: an overlay hidden or removed since the last paint, a layout root replaced via setLayoutRoot, or a component removed from a Container mid-gesture must stop receiving press/drag/release events immediately (the cached layout frame only refreshes on the next paint). PR #197 deliberately changes the ownership of long-user bubble text rows: the bubble itself, in both collapsed and expanded states, is now a Host disclosure target — ordinary rows that display canonical user text and were previously selection-owned. Those specific user-text rows therefore no longer promise double-click word selection: the first complete plain click runs the local expand/collapse action. X055.title: Viewport growth must not re-arm follow-end
X055.why: ScrollView re-arms follow-end whenever a layout clamp lands the scroll on the new maximum, interpreting that as 'the user's position caught up to the bottom'. That holds when the CONTENT shrank (a fold/collapse). It is wrong when the VIEWPORT grew (pinned chrome rows appearing/disappearing, terminal resize): maxScrollTop shrinks without any content change, so a user who had deliberately scrolled away from the tail is silently pulled back to it. The pinned fullscreen queue pane is a concrete trigger: a queued occurrence's create/remove changes the transcript viewport height. The host cannot compensate reliably (the alt screen owns the wheel/keyboard/scrollbar gestures after the host router sees them, and an overlay may consume the wheel), so the rule belongs in the viewport layer. When a content shrink and a viewport growth coincide in one layout pass, the viewport growth wins — the structural screen-capacity change dominates the clamp inference.

X056.title: Overlay operation and focus-transition supersession seam
X056.why: The host temporarily suppresses a set of managed overlays (a Question / Save Location modal, or a fullscreen screen swap) and later restores them. Upstream setHidden(false) and focus() promote the overlay's visual order AND take keyboard focus as side effects, so an internal restore would raise a restored capturing overlay above a nonCapturing HUD that legitimately sat above it, and would fire spurious onFocus/onBlur on an overlay the plugin deliberately blurred. The fork adds the minimal opt-in seam so an internal restore reproduces the pre-suppression stacking and keyboard ownership: `preserveOrder`/`preserveFocus` on setHidden, and `initialFocus: false` on showOverlay for the fullscreen rebind. The same supersession rule applies inside the fork's focus core: Tui.setFocusInternal runs the previous component's onBlur synchronously BEFORE installing the next focus, so an onBlur that re-requests focus (or mounts another overlay) would be overwritten by the outer transition. A monotonic focus revision lets the outer transition detect that a newer one superseded it and leave the newer transaction's state in place. A pending transition must also survive an onBlur that mutates the pending target itself (blur/hide/close) WITHOUT starting a new focus transition: the fork records the released target so the outer transition re-derives instead of installing a released/hidden/removed node.

X058.title: Viewport passthrough for a focused capturing overlay
X058.why: The host transcript-search box is a capturing overlay: it must keep KEYBOARD focus (typing must reach its Input, Esc/Ctrl+F/Enter are fixed overlay contracts), so `nonCapturing` is not an option. But while it is open the user must still be able to move around the transcript they are searching: wheel / Alt+wheel, PageUp/PageDown, scrollbar hover/drag, and background text selection outside the box. Upstream ties ALL of those to `hasOverlay()` / `isOverlayFocused()`: a focused overlay blocks the wheel, PageUp and PageDown (the early viewport-key return), `getScrollbarTargetAt` returns undefined whenever ANY overlay is visible, and the selection-anchor scrollView lookup is skipped under any overlay. A host-only implementation cannot restore those: the scrollbar hit-test/drag and the selection anchor live entirely inside TuiAltScreen, and reimplementing them in the host would duplicate pointer ownership rather than narrow it. The seam is therefore one optional boolean with a single predicate pair, and every non-opted-in overlay keeps the upstream behavior byte-for-byte.

X059.title: Stateful OSC 9;4 projection and terminal-specific heartbeat
X059.why: Tern derives an Agent 'waiting_input' state from OSC 9;4 'paused' (9;4;4), which the boolean Terminal.setProgress(active) cannot express: false means idle, so a host that wants to show a user-blocked wait would have to write a clear first (a visible working -> idle -> waiting_input blink), and ProcessTerminal.stop() would not know that a physical state is still on the pane. The fork therefore keeps the boolean contract as-is and adds one optional stateful projection whose physical state is tracked independently of the keepalive timer. The same physical state machine also owns the active heartbeat: the logical unknown-progress working state is always projected as OSC 9;4 state 1 value 0, which keeps the pane working without forcing the strong indeterminate animation of state 3, while 'paused' remains 9;4;4. The periodic refresh is only required by terminals known to expire that state; repeating it on a persistent terminal is unnecessary and may restart their native progress animation.

Terminal.setProgressState?(state) — optional and additive; an implementation that does not provide it keeps the boolean contract unchanged.

ProcessTerminal.setProgressState: 'indeterminate' ALWAYS writes OSC 9;4;1;0 once per explicit projection and starts the 1 s heartbeat only on a terminal known to expire OSC 9;4 state (currently Ghostty / Monstar); 'paused' stops the heartbeat and writes OSC 9;4;4 with NO intermediate 9;4;0; 'clear' stops the heartbeat and writes OSC 9;4;0.

shouldKeepTerminalProgressAlive(env) is the positive allowlist for that heartbeat, snapshotted once at ProcessTerminal construction; persistent terminals (Tern, Kitty, WezTerm, Windows Terminal, unknown) receive no periodic 9;4;1;0 refresh.
A repeated explicit projection still writes its own bytes and starts no second interval.

ProcessTerminal.stop() clears EVERY non-clear physical progress state, not only a heartbeat-backed one, so a paused state cannot leak into the shell or an $EDITOR that takes the terminal next.

X063.title: A read-only Down-boundary seam on the Editor's own visual-line classifier
X063.why: The host's Task Quick on-demand entry (Phase 3B/B4-B) must fire on a Down press at the editor's last VISUAL line only. The visual boundary lives entirely inside the fork editor: soft word-wrap, CJK/astral width, empty lines, history browsing, autocomplete, jump mode and bracketed paste all change what Down means, and the private word-wrap map (`buildVisualLineMap` + `findCurrentVisualLine`) plus the private mode flags are the only authoritative classifier. The host cannot re-derive it from the public surface — a `cursor.line === lastLine` or character-count guess answers the LOGICAL line, not the wrapped one, and re-implementing the wrap would drift from the exact layout the user sees. Upstream has no such seam.
changedSurface: `protected canYieldDownAtLastVisualLine(expectedLayoutWidth: number): boolean` — one synchronous, read-only, side-effect-free method on the fork `Editor`.

`public onVisualLineBoundaryChanged?(reason: 'navigation' | 'autocomplete' | 'history' | 'paste' | 'programmatic', onLastVisualLine: boolean): void` - an observation-only callback fired after every editor transition that can change the Down-admission fact; the payload is the transition CLASS plus the post-transition raw boundary state: navigation moves (Up/Down/PageUp/PageDown with the post-move state read off the move's own wrap map; Left/Right, word/line jumps, character jump and mouse repositioning), the AUTOCOMPLETE open/close flips (a dropdown refuses Down with no cursor move — both directions notify, including an open/close pair whose visual-line truth is unchanged), dedicated history recall, bracketed-paste completion, and programmatic setText/setTextAndCursor/setCursor. The payload is the TRANSITION CLASS (navigation/autocomplete/history/paste/programmatic), never a content value: two events may carry the same visual-line truth and still flip the admission, so the host recomposes per event without equality gating (the base editor exposes no caret-change callback for a boundary that is a wrap-map fact, not a document fact).

True only when `lastWidth === expectedLayoutWidth`, the cursor is on the last VISUAL line of the editor's own wrap map, and NO transient mode owns Down: `historyIndex === -1`, `autocompleteState === null`, `jumpMode === null`, `isInPaste === false`.
`expectedLayoutWidth` must be the SAME layout width `render()` derived for the painted frame, so a stale caller width can never classify against a wrap map the user is not looking at.

No private field becomes public, no wrap logic is duplicated, and the editor's own key routing, cursor and document are untouched: the callback is an observation whose payload is computed from the moving code's OWN wrap-map facts (page moves publish theirs; Left/Right reuse the pre-move read plus one post-move comparison), so the notify adds no second wrap-map build on any navigation path.

The host `TuiEditor` subclass exposes `canEnterTaskQuickFromDown(physicalWidth)` on top of the seam (host-side code, not this ledger). Both fork deltas serve the same host consumer — the read-only classifier and the state-carrying observation callback; no other fork surface changed.

items: The seam reads only existing private state (`lastWidth`, `buildVisualLineMap`, `findCurrentVisualLine`, `historyIndex`, `autocompleteState`, `jumpMode`, `isInPaste`) through the existing private methods `isOnLastVisualLine` uses — no vendored caller behavior changes and no vendored component consumes the method.

The lazy one-shot call shape (one wrap-map computation per CANDIDATE Down, per the host predicate's guard chain) keeps ordinary printable-key input paths free of any new editor content scan. The notification adds NO second wrap-map build on any navigation path (page moves and cursor moves publish their own map facts; the shared notify consumes them), and the autocomplete event fires only on the OPEN flip — a suggestion refresh while the picker is already open costs no scan. A mode flip or programmatic replacement pays ONE authoritative rebuild for its notify; that is the event's own cost, not a per-keystroke scan.
vendorInternal.notes: No vendor-internal consumer exists; the fork method is consumed exclusively through the host subclass.

items: Exactly one inheritance edge relies on the seam: `TuiEditor extends Editor` (`src/tui/interaction/tui-editor.ts`) calls the protected method from `canEnterTaskQuickFromDown`. No other subclass exists in the bundle, and the method is `protected`, so it is invisible to every non-subclass consumer including the public Extension API.
inheritanceStructural.notes: The structural edge is the intended contract: a read-only capability granted to the first-party subclass only.

items: `src/tui/interaction/tui-editor.ts` — `canEnterTaskQuickFromDown(physicalWidth)` derives the layout width with the SAME rule `render()` uses (`max(1, physicalWidth - 2 * getPaddingX())`), requires prompt input mode, and delegates the rest to the seam.

`src/tui-app.ts` — the single private `quickDownEligible()` predicate calls it ONLY when the host editor is the real focused component with no higher-priority owner; the local bool alone never routes input.
host.notes: The host consumes the seam through one guarded predicate; the seam never decides routing by itself.

items: The method is `protected` on the vendored `Editor` class and is NOT re-exported, declared, or reachable through the package entry (`src/index.ts`) or any public structural type — the public Extension Editor API is unchanged.
publicExtension.notes: No public surface change: a plugin editor sees the same class shape as before.

items: an empty editor and a cursor at the end of the last line yield true on a live painted frame
a hard-multiline draft answers false above the last visual line and true only after Down reaches it
a soft-wrapped single logical line answers false on middle segments and true only on the last segment (the boundary a logical-line classifier gets wrong)
history browsing, an open autocomplete dropdown, armed jump mode and an in-flight bracketed paste each force false, and return to true only when the editor itself leaves the mode
a caller width that does not match the painted frame's layout width forces false until the frame is repainted at that width
the seam consumes nothing: a real Down after a false answer still moves the cursor natively

the boundary-notification callback fires with the TRANSITION CLASS on every admission-affecting transition — navigation moves (Up/Down/Page always; Left/Right including the hard logical-line-end wrap, with the intra-line walk dispatching as a cheap drop the host re-reads), the programmatic setCursor/setTextAndCursor replacements — while printable input never dispatches and the document, cursor and key routing stay untouched; the autocomplete open flip and close flip notify distinctly from navigation; and the notify consumes the moving code's own published wrap-map facts instead of a second build

The fork adds exactly that protected seam PLUS the observation-only `onVisualLineBoundaryChanged` callback that fires with the transition class and the post-move boundary state after EVERY navigation move (each move publishes its own wrap-map facts; a no-flip move's event is a cheap drop) and after every admission mode flip (autocomplete open/close, jump arm/cancel, history recall, paste completion), so the host can keep its painted hint fresh; the wrapping, history, autocomplete, jump and paste behavior are upstream's own, unchanged.
